author: reek
body: A panel must have a visible extent, and on the GPU backend it had none.

author: reek
body: Every built-in theme gives its panel style a background equal to the page background and a one-pixel border, so the border is the only thing that delineates a panel at all. The CPU renderer draws it -- render-panel calls render-border, and so do the gauge, button and input paths. The GPU renderer emitted the fill and dropped the border, so on the backend every bare-metal app actually uses, a panel painted its parent's colour onto its parent and disappeared. That is why the GuiOS sidebar and taskbar had no extent while the depth rule was correct and the triangle count was healthy: the geometry was submitted, it was in front, and it was the same colour as what it covered.

author: reek
body: Neither the triangle count nor gpu-depth-tree can see this. Both backends agreed on the fill, so a rect was always emitted; what differed was one the theme asked for and only one backend drew. The instrument has to read pixels and it has to look for the border colour specifically.

author: reek
body: The probe tree carries no separator, which is the whole reason it is shaped this way: a separator paints pal-border too, so its presence would make this count non-zero whatever the panel does. With it absent, pal-border in the framebuffer can only have come from a panel border. Run against a renderer without the fix the count is zero.

author: reek
body: The scan strides eight columns and every row. A border is one pixel wide, so a column stride crosses the vertical edges and a row stride could step over the horizontal ones. Counting rather than sampling a computed coordinate keeps the test honest when layout moves.
